meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade changed before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. People draft in another program and paste it in, so what does that prove? You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
That's one record, and Owen hasn't been asked about it. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote. They pull lines from critics and study guides all the time. Does his essay say the line is Shakespeare's, or does it just put it in quotation marks?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
That's your opinion of the line. I asked whether the essay presents it as Shakespeare's, yes or no.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Outlines change. A student who thinks harder lands somewhere new, and that's called revising. Is the October 15 date on the outline itself?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight. But you haven't answered whether the October 15 date is on the outline itself, and I'm not agreeing to anything until you do.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday depends on the writing, and I'm not answering for Owen until I have it. Revising explains the outline. What explains a line that isn't in the play?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and your private supervised rewrite offer put in writing, with a statement that nothing goes on Owen's record, and I want answers to what I asked you in the room. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She finished at her fallback position, accepting that your rewrite offer met her demand for no record, but agreeing to nothing and still wanting it in writing plus answers; that offer is the fair outcome, and time did not run out before it came.
What moved her: Owning the zero before calling home in your first sentence earned a flat okay, because it answered her procedure complaint before she had to press it.
What cost ground: Leaving her question about whether Owen was spoken to before the zero unanswered kept her suspicious and made every later document look like a case built after the fact.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your version history with its late-night times on October 28 came close to that night, which is why she went shorter and harder, but it proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether Owen was spoken to, answer plainly that he was not and that you are fixing that, then show the outline with its date before she has to ask for it.
